---
title: "The propagation gate: what bioc-registry publishes, and why"
date: 2026-08-04
date-modified: 2026-09-30
---

r-universe and bioc-build build Bioconductor packages. Only some of those builds become what
[bioc-registry](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-registry) publishes: installable repositories
at `https://bioc-registry.seandavi.workers.dev/repo/{bioc,bioc-release}`, and the propagation
index that the [`/next/` preview pages](astro-site-build.qmd) are built from. This page states
the rule that decides, read from the code that runs it.

::: {.callout-important}
## This gate does not govern bioconductor.org today
bioconductor.org's repositories and package pages do not read from bioc-registry. Packages
reach bioconductor.org through Bioconductor's own propagation (below) and the hourly
`bioc-sync` from master; its landing pages take versions and download links from the
repositories' own `PACKAGES` indexes. Switching bioconductor.org's software repositories to
bioc-registry is a documented plan with open blockers: [Registry switch](registry-switch.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Bioconductor's production gate is a different gate
Bioconductor's production propagation to `bioconductor.org` runs in core infrastructure next
to BBS and is known here only from conversation. It is described on
[Propagation in the legacy system](legacy-propagation.qmd), together with the push hooks and
the measured agreement between r-universe's checks and `nebbiolo1`'s. The two are compared at
the [end of this page](#relation-to-the-legacy-production-gate).
:::

## The gate, check by check

Since [ADR 0011](adr/0011-one-propagation-gate-for-every-producer.md) (2026-09-04) there is one
decision function, `gate()` in
[`src/repo.ts`](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-registry/blob/f10719e/src/repo.ts#L677-L723),
with three callers and no gating anywhere else:

| Caller | Producer | Config |
|---|---|---|
| `evaluate()` in [`src/index.ts`](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-registry/blob/f10719e/src/index.ts#L536-L589), on every r-universe wave | r-universe | gating R from `config.yaml`, `replace_seed: false` |
| `POST /publish` (maintenance key required) | bioc-build | the R version bioc-build's image ships, `replace_seed: true`, plus manifest rules |
| `POST /gate` (public, read-only) | whatever the caller sends | defaults as for r-universe |

Everything below is read from bioc-registry at commit `f10719e` (main, 2026-09-28). A
candidate propagates when **every** rule passes. Each decision returns every rule's verdict,
pass or fail, under these names:

1. **`build-status`**: the producer's build status is `success`. For r-universe that is
   `_status`; `_failure` is not read. A green status on a stale commit is caught by
   `version-gate` in practice, because the stale version has already propagated.
   Before the gate runs, `evaluate()` drops any r-universe package with no source sha256.
2. **`families`**: at least one platform family passes, judged only on jobs running the
   gating R version. The gating R is resolved at evaluation time from
   `bioconductor.org/config.yaml` (`r_ver_for_bioc_ver` for the universe's Bioconductor
   version) and matched against each job's actual R version, not its label. Three families
   are gated ([`passingFamilies`](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-registry/blob/f10719e/src/repo.ts#L223-L232)):
   `linux` (the `source` job plus `linux-*` x86_64), `win` (`windows-*` x86_64) and `mac`
   (`macos-*` arm64). A family passes when it has at least one gating job and none of them is
   `ERROR`, `FAIL` or `FAILURE`. `NOTE` and `WARNING` pass. Other configs gate nothing:
   `bioc-checks`, `wasm`, linux arm64, mac x86_64. bioc-build reports one `linux-x86_64` job.
3. **`bioccheck`**: advisory in every caller today; it always passes and records the
   verdict. A caller could set it to `blocking`, and then `ERROR`/`FAIL` would block.
4. **`version-parse`**: the version is digits separated by `.` or `-`.
5. **`version-gate`**: the version is a strict bump over the one in the propagation index,
   or the package is new. A push without a bump never propagates. With `replace_seed`
   (bioc-build only), a build at the same version may also replace a `bioconductor` seed;
   r-universe must bump.
6. **`manifest-state`, `manifest-git-url`, `manifest-stream`, `manifest-component`**
   (bioc-build only): the package's entry in
   [bioc-manifest](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-manifest), read at the commit the build
   recorded, is `active`, names the git URL that was built, lists the build's stream, and has
   `component` equal to `profile`.
7. **`deps`**, run last over everything the other rules cleared
   ([`approveByDeps`](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-registry/blob/f10719e/src/repo.ts#L600-L641)):
   every `Depends`, `Imports` and `LinkingTo` entry naming a package that is itself in the
   propagation index must be present at a version meeting its `>=` or `>` constraint.
   Dependencies not in the index (CRAN, base R, and annotation, experiment and workflow
   packages until they have a build home) pass untouched. Candidates are approved in waves
   until a fixpoint, so a package lands as soon as what it waits on does. A dependency that is
   in neither the index nor CRAN is not caught; that is
   [bioc-registry#56](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-registry/issues/56) (open), and
   finding 2 on [Registry switch](registry-switch.qmd).

What propagates for an r-universe package that passes: the **source tarball always**;
**binaries only for the families that passed**, and only those built at the same version with
status `success`. `wasm` binaries ride along with no gate of their own. The passing families
are recorded on the index entry as `archs`, the BiocCheck verdict as `bioccheck`.

Every new version that fails (its `version-gate` passed, something else did not) is written
to `prop/{universe}/blocked/` with its full list of rule verdicts. To ask why a package did
not propagate, or whether it would, `POST /gate` runs the same function against the live
index and writes nothing:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://bioc-registry.seandavi.workers.dev/gate \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"universe":"bioc-release","candidates":[{"package":"limma","version":"99.0.0",
       "jobs":[{"config":"source","r":"4.6.0","check":"OK"}]}]}'
# 2026-09-30: propagate true, archs ["linux"], gating_r 4.6, "99.0.0 > 3.68.5"
```

What this gate does **not** check, and the [legacy production gate or the push hooks](legacy-propagation.qmd) do:

- The `nebbiolo1` sha match. The gate has no provenance check for r-universe builds.
  (bioc-build's sha256 and `gh attestation verify` are checked by its publisher; per ADR 0011
  they are integrity checks, not gate rules.)
- The push-hook rules: version parity, `x` and `y` unchanged, the 5 MiB file limit, merge
  markers. It inherits them by trusting that the commit reached `git.bioconductor.org`.

### Binaries that arrive after publication

The gate decides binaries in the wave that first publishes a version, and `version-gate` keeps
that version out of every later wave. Since bioc-registry#50 (PR #51, merged 2026-09-29
02:30 UTC), every wave ends with a top-up
([`topUpBinaries`](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-registry/blob/f10719e/src/repo.ts#L268-L288),
[`topUp`](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-registry/blob/f10719e/src/index.ts#L700-L722)):

- For an r-universe entry, if r-universe now has a successful binary **at the published
  version** for a family that passed then or passes now on the gating R, it is added. This
  covers binaries that finish after the source was published and platforms whose check passes
  on a same-version rebuild.
- For a seeded entry, Bioconductor's binaries are fetched once they reach the seeded version.

Top-up is additive only: the source, its sha256 and the version never change, a family that
passed is never withdrawn, and a slot that already has a binary keeps it. Each addition is
recorded under `prop/{universe}/topup/`. `POST /topup` (maintenance key) runs the same for a
backfill.

## Three ways into the index

Each index entry carries an `origin`:

| `origin` | How it got there | `bioc` (devel) | `bioc-release` |
|---|---|--:|--:|
| `r-universe` (or no field: entries from before the field existed) | passed the gate above; `archs` says on which families | 2,292 | 2,235 |
| `bioconductor` | **seeded**, never faced the gate; empty `archs`, null `bioccheck` | 124 | 153 |
| `bioc-build` | passed the gate through `POST /publish` | 2 | 2 |

Counts from the live index, 2026-09-30.

Seeds exist because some packages build in BBS and fail in r-universe's environment, usually
because an example reaches a network service the runner cannot (about 300 when measured
2026-08-04; 277 seeded entries today). They are copied from Bioconductor's repository for the
universe's branch: the devel repository for `bioc`, the release repository for
`bioc-release` (`seedPlan()` in `src/index.ts`). Seeding only fills holes. A seed is replaced
by an r-universe build when the maintainer bumps the version, or by a bioc-build build at the
same version.

## What r-universe already computes

A common assumption, encouraged by "r-universe doesn't care about `R CMD check`", is that
r-universe skips checking. It does not. It **does not gate** on the result, which is a
different claim. It runs `R CMD check` on every platform in its matrix, and for Bioconductor
packages it also runs **BiocCheck**.

All of it is exposed in the per-package API, e.g.
`https://bioc.r-universe.dev/api/packages/limma` (verified live, 2026-08-04):

| Field | Contents |
|---|---|
| `_jobs[]` | one entry per matrix leg: `{job, time, config, r, check, artifact}`. `config` values include `source`, `bioc-checks`, `linux-{devel,release}-{arm64,x86_64}`, `macos-*`, `windows-*`, `wasm-release`. `check` is `OK` / `NOTE` / `WARNING` / `ERROR` / `FAIL`. |
| `_bioccheck` | BiocCheck summary as counts: `{error, warning, note}`. First-class API field; no download required. |
| `_commit` | `{id, author, committer, message, time}`: the source commit sha and metadata. |
| `_status` | overall deploy status for the package. |
| `_failure` | present when the **newest** commit failed to produce a source package. |
| `_buildurl` | the GitHub Actions **run** URL, in `r-universe/{universe}`. |
| `_binaries[]` | per-artifact provenance: `{r, os, arch, distro, version, date, commit, fileid, status, check, buildurl}`. |

Build logs and the full BiocCheck artifact are retrievable without authentication via
`/api/actions/logs/{job}` and `/api/actions/artifacts/{id}` (both 302 to a signed blob URL).

The gate therefore does not need to run checks. It needs to **read** them.

## Why the registry polls

r-universe emits **no webhook, no `repository_dispatch`, and no subscribable status
endpoint**. The feature request for build notifications
([`r-universe-org/help#101`](https://github.com/r-universe-org/help/issues/101)) is open with
no comments (checked 2026-09-30). The one push-style signal, a GitHub commit status on the
upstream repo (context `r-universe/{universe}/{package}/deploy`), needs the r-universe GitHub
App installed on that repo; checked against `bioc/limma` on 2026-08-04 at the sha r-universe
built, there were no statuses.

So the registry polls. Its Worker cron runs every 15 minutes (`*/15 * * * *` in
`wrangler.jsonc`). Each run fetches `/api/packages` for both universes with a fixed field list
and hashes the response; a new wave (gate, propagate, top-up) starts only when the hash
changes. The field list leaves out volatile fields such as `_stars` so the hash stays quiet
when nothing build-relevant changed. The same cron also captures logs and compacts the
observation archive.

For scale: r-universe discovers new commits once an hour (`sync.yml` in
`r-universe-org/control-room`, cron `25 * * * *`, checked 2026-09-30), and rebuilds nightly
(`rebuilds.yml`, `30 1 * * *`). Measured against `bioc-release` on 2026-08-04, `/api/files`
with `fields=_created,_buildurl,_commit` was 1.1 MB in 0.27 s; `/api/packages` with a field
list 6.4 MB in 0.9 s; with no field list about 69 MB. Always pass `fields=`.
`PATCH /api/sync` is public, unauthenticated, and self-throttles to 60 seconds, if a sync is
needed ahead of the cron.

### Two traps in the data

**`_status` can be green on a stale commit.** When the newest commit fails to produce a source
package, the package keeps its previous successful `_status` and the failure appears separately
in `_failure`. A gate reading only `_status` will propagate while the current head is broken.
This gate reads only `_status` and relies on `version-gate` (rule 1 above).

**Key the delta on `_commit.id`, not build time.** 453 release packages were rebuilt in the
24 hours before the 2026-08-04 measurement, but r-universe also rebuilds on dependency
changes, R-version changes, the nightly rebuild cron, and a reverse-dependency cascade after
any version change. Most of that churn carries no new source.

## Relation to the legacy production gate

| | Legacy production gate | This gate |
|---|---|---|
| Feeds | `bioconductor.org/packages/...` (the site and its mirrors) | `bioc-registry` (`/repo/...`, the propagation index, the `/next/` pages) |
| Runs in | Bioconductor core infrastructure, alongside BBS | a Cloudflare Worker |
| Described from | conversation with a core team member, 2026-08-04, not re-verified since | the code, pinned at commit [`f10719e`](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-registry/tree/f10719e) |
| Provenance check | source sha must match what `nebbiolo1` built | none for r-universe: pushes to `git.bioconductor.org` are assumed hook-checked upstream |
| Check verdict | "the check is clean": one all-or-nothing verdict; the source does not say it covers more than one platform | per platform family on the gating R; at least one family must pass |
| Version rule | version must match `nebbiolo1`'s build | strict bump over the last propagated version |
| Dependency rule | unknown | hard deps that this registry publishes must be satisfiable |
| BiocCheck | advisory | advisory, recorded on the index entry |
| Late binaries | unknown | added by top-up at the same version |

Whether `WARNINGS` counts as clean in the legacy gate is still [undetermined](legacy-propagation.qmd#what-could-not-be-determined);
this gate answers it explicitly (`families`: yes).
